author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Israeli forces have intensified military operations across the occupied West Bank, forcibly displacing more than 2,000 Palestinians in Hebron, nearly half of them children. The governor says 400 families have been expelled from their homes following a shooting on Friday that killed two Israeli soldiers. On the third day of the assault, Israeli forces have demolished homes and businesses, while displaced families seek shelter with relatives and friends. Near Jenin, residents of an entire Palestinian village have been ordered to leave permanently, threatening their homes, farmland and livelihoods. Human rights organisations warn that the forced displacement of Palestinian communities is systematic and are calling for international intervention. Israel has also imposed additional movement restrictions, including a ban on Palestinians entering the Jordan Valley, citing security preparations ahead of Tuesday's Israeli elections. 

Al Jazeera's Nour Odeh reports from Ramallah.
Jasper Nathan

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Almost 159 million voters can cast ballots in Brazil’s presidential runoff on Sunday. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term and is running against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a right-wing candidate and the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.

The vote could shift Brazil’s global alliances. Lula has strengthened ties with China and the Global South, while Bolsonaro has signalled closer alignment with the United States.

Paulo Sotero, a distinguished fellow and former director of the Brazil Institute at the Wilson Centre, says democracy is at stake. He describes Lula as an experienced politician from the left and the union movement, who ran in many elections, served three terms as president, and never did anything to undermine democracy.

Sotero calls Flávio Bolsonaro “a mystery”, a senator who has never presented a single bill and is a very inactive politician.
